alexa.p: Quick async heads-up — I'm onboarding Ceres-7B to hosted. Weights uploaded to s3://redwood-models/ceres-7b/v1/ (sha256: a3f9...). Tokenizer seems to emit an extra BOS sometimes when using the HF tokenizer binary; observed duplicated leading token on a few samples. Also need kernel/CUDA checks: buildbase currently CUDA 12.5 + Triton 2.1 in the container. Can someone confirm compatibility and whether we should rebuild the container with cuda12.6?

matt.k: Thanks — I'll run a quick kernel probe on the canary infra. If it's a BOS duplication it's often the tokenizer config (add_special_tokens) or an off-by-one in the generate wrapper. Do you have a minimal repro?

alexa.p: Minimal repro: ran python snippet locally:```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('redwood/ceres-7b-tokenizer')
print(t.encode("Hello"))
```
Sometimes returns `[50256, 10]` and sometimes `[1, 50256, 10]` (where 1 is BOS). Not deterministic across runs (we think because of hf tokenizer fallback path).

sophie: Seen this before with tokenizers where we ship both fast + slow and HF falls back to slow on some machines. Either force use_fast=True or set `add_bos_token=False` in our serving tokenizer wrapper. I'd prefer a wrapper fix so models are robust across envs.

raj: For weights: do we have both fp16 and int8 quant artifacts? I only see `ceres-7b-v1-fp16.safetensors` and `ceres-7b-v1-pt-int8.safetensors` in the S3 path. If we rely on int8 runtime kernels might differ (some kernels don't support fused quant ops).

jules: I checked the runtime matrix: Ceres-7B needs sm86 kernels for our fused attention path in quantized mode. CUDA12.5 should be fine on our gpu fleet but Triton 2.1 has a known issue with the NVTX kernel selection causing mis-matches on cuda12.5 on certain driver levels. We should either bump Triton to 2.2 or rebuild the container with explicit kernel fallback enabled.

maya: Rebuild cost/impact: if we rebuild base -> triggers all model containers to rebuild, which is heavy. Alternative: create per-model runtime overlay that pins Triton 2.2 + kernel patches just for Ceres. That's what we did for Atlas-2.7b.

alexa.p: Good call. For now can we do two things: (1) Sophie, can you add a tokenizer override in the model config so serving forces `use_fast=True` and sets `bos_token=None`? (2) Matt/Jules/Maya, run kernel probe on canary with Triton 2.2 and with current 2.1 + kernel-fallback env var to see perf/regression. I'll open a canary test PR afterwards.

matt.k: On it. Pinging infra probe script:```bash
./tools/kernel_probe.sh --model ceres-7b --triton 2.1 --cuda 12.5 --out /tmp/ceres-probe-2.1.txt
./tools/kernel_probe.sh --model ceres-7b --triton 2.2 --cuda 12.5 --out /tmp/ceres-probe-2.2.txt
```
I'll attach diffs.

sophie: I'll add the tokenizer config patch, small change in model card `tokenizer_overrides: {use_fast: true, add_bos_token: false}` — sending a tiny PR in a bit. Also adding a compatibility test to the model-evals to assert no leading bos in top-5 samples.

jules: Ran quick synthetic locally — with Triton 2.1 hit a kernel selection warning for fused-attn on one canary (log snippet: `warning: no compatible kernel for sm86/fused_attn_int8, falling back to generic kernel`). With Triton 2.2 the warning disappears but latency slightly higher on that node (noisy neighbor). We'll need to compare p99s on canary.

maya: Pushed an overlay image recipe that installs triton==2.2 and sets `TRITON_ENABLE_KERNEL_FALLBACK=1`. CI will build. If that looks stable we can ship overlay only for ceres.

deploy-bot: Build queued: `build-overlay-ceres-1999998888` started (job id: 78232).

ci-bot: build-overlay-ceres-1999998888: FAILED — missing system lib `libnvrtc.so.12` in base image. See logs: `/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libnvrtc.so.12: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`

matt.k: Ah — base image was `nvidia/cuda:12.5-runtime-ubuntu22.04` which doesn't include nvrtc12 in that tag. We either need runtime with `-devel` or switch to `12.6` base. Rebuilding with `nvidia/cuda:12.6-runtime-ubuntu22.04` should fix. I'll kick off variant builds.

alexa.p: Thanks. Sounds like action items: Sophie PR for tokenizer override, Matt to rebuild overlay with cuda12.6 base, Jules to run perf p99 numbers, Maya to keep overlay small and only target Ceres. I'll open a tracking ticket and assign owners.

raj: One more Q — if int8 artifact is used and we don't have fused kernels, do we auto-fallback to fp16 path? We should ensure the routing policy prefers fp16 on nodes without fused kernel support.

jules: Good catch. We can add a model runtime policy: `preferred_variant_order: [fp16, int8]` until we validate int8 path on all fleets. Add it to the model manifest in the PR.

alexa.p: Perfect. Thanks everyone — please drop short updates in this thread as you hit each step. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: build-overlay-ceres-1999998888: SUCCESS on cuda12.6 variant (job id: 78233)

matt.k: Overlay image built and pushed to gcr.io/redwood/ceres-overlay:triton2.2-cuda12.6. Running kernel probe now, will post results in a few mins.

jules: Perf note: preliminary p99 on canary with overlay is +8% vs baseline but stable. We'll decide whether that's acceptable or we delay int8 rollout.

sophie: PR merged for tokenizer overrides and model manifest updated with preferred_variant_order.

alexa.p: Great — closing loop. If we see production weirdness we can revert to fp16-only.

maya: I'll schedule a small canary rollout tomorrow 06:00 UTC.

alexa.p: Awesome, thanks all.

matt.k: probe logs attached to ticket — no kernel errors with 2.2 + cuda12.6 on tested nodes.

alexa.p: :thumbsup:
